substantive_reconstruction.basis_and_growth: For occupation f with sum n there are m_f=n!/product f_i! distinct product-basis words. Their normalized uniform sum has norm1. Different occupations have disjoint word supports, and invariance under every permutation means coefficients are constant on each such orbit. This proves both orthogonality and spanning, not just a tuple count. Stars and bars then gives binom(n+d-1,d-1). The product formula has degree d-1 and leading coefficient1/(d-1)! at fixed d>=1. For d>=2 the ratio against d^n has successive-term limit1/d<1 and tends to zero. At d1 it remains one. At n0 the tensor unit has dimension one even for d0; at d0,n>0 both spaces have dimension zero and there is no density operator or meaningful0/0 fraction. The corrected final paragraph compares ambient Hilbert-space dimension d^n, not a finite number of all quantum states, which form an uncountable set.
substantive_reconstruction.support_and_purification: The two-qubit singlet projector is fixed under swap conjugation but killed by the symmetric projector. I_4/4 gives a mixed counterexample with nonzero antisymmetric weight. For invariant rho choose UNNORMALIZED Omega=sum_w |w>|w> and Psi=(sqrt(rho) tensor I)Omega. Its norm squared is tr rho=1 and tracing the reference returns rho. Functional calculus makes sqrt(rho) commute with every permutation Q; product-basis permutation matrices are real, so (Q tensor Q)Omega=Omega. Regrouping A1...AnR1...Rn as paired A_iR_i systems puts Psi in Sym^n(C^d tensor C^d), with local dimension d^2. The pure symmetric de Finetti theorem is an input here: applying it on paired systems and tracing references yields a mixture of mixed product states, with trace norm error no greater by channel contractivity. This does not put the original rho in Sym^n(C^d) or reprove the complete de Finetti theorem.
substantive_reconstruction.ratio_quantifiers: The exact product q_d(m)/q_d(m+k)=product_j (m+j)/(m+k+j) proves the asymptotic regime. For fixed d>=2, k=o(m) makes each factor tend to one. Conversely every factor is at most one and the product is at most its largest factor (m+d-1)/(m+k+d-1), so a product limit1 forces k/m to zero. At k/m->c>0 the limit is(1+c)^(-(d-1)); at unbounded ratio it is zero. d2,k=m gives1/2, refuting closeness from polynomial dimension alone. d1 is the empty-product exception. For cloning put M=N+k; a fixed difference or o(N) yields closeness, whereas M/N->c>1 does not at d>=2. Mixed de Finetti uses the squared local dimension. These are independently derived ratios, not reliance on ambiguous extracted source typography.
substantive_reconstruction.cloning_and_full_algebra: K is CP and its outputs are symmetric-supported by compression. Set A=tr_{M-N}Pi_M. Every fully symmetric M-vector is symmetric on the first N factors, so A=Pi_N A Pi_N. Unitary invariance and irreducibility of Sym^N force A=(q_d(M)/q_d(N))Pi_N by its trace. Hence tr K(X)=tr(Pi_N X), which is trace preservation only on symmetric-supported inputs, and trace nonincrease for general positive X. At d2,N=M2 the singlet is sent to zero. The complement functional X->tr((I-Pi_N)X) is positive and hence CP into scalars; multiplying by an output density sigma is CP, so adding it produces a full CPTP completion. Its nonsymmetric output can be nonzero if the complement input exists and sigma is nonsymmetric. A symmetric sigma supplies a symmetric-range completion, not a theorem about every completion. For N0/1 or d1 the whole input already equals its symmetric space. Division through zero-dimensional positive powers is excluded.
